claim: For any fixed \(r\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}\) and every \(\lambda>0\), the square-lattice operator \(H_{\lambda,r}=4I-\sum_{|e|_1=1}T_e-\lambda|0\rangle\langle0|+\lambda|r\rangle\langle r|\) on \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z^2)\) has exactly one simple eigenvalue below \([0,8]\) and exactly one simple eigenvalue above \([0,8]\), situated at \(-\kappa_r(\lambda)\) and \(8+\kappa_r(\lambda)\), respectively. With \(h(k)=4-2\cos k_1-2\cos k_2\), \(G_s(\kappa)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^2}\cos(k\cdot s)/(h(k)+\kappa)\,dk/(2\pi)^2\), and \(R_r=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^2}(1-\cos(k\cdot r))/h(k)\,dk/(2\pi)^2>0\), \(\kappa_r\) is the unique positive solution of \(\lambda^2\left(G_0(\kappa)^2-G_r(\kappa)^2\right)=1\) and satisfies \(\kappa_r(\lambda)=32\exp(-2\pi R_r)\exp(-2\pi/(R_r\lambda^2))(1+o(1))\) as \(\lambda\downarrow0\). For nearest-neighbor \(r=(1,0)\), \(R_r=1/4\), hence \(\kappa_r(\lambda)\sim32e^{-\pi/2}e^{-8\pi/\lambda^2}\).

correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization shows spectrum [0,8]. The rank-two eigenproblem has determinant 1-lambda^2(G0-Gr)(G0+Gr). Both strictly positive factors strictly decrease; the product decreases from infinity to zero, giving precisely one simple negative eigenvalue. The checkerboard-reflection unitary maps H to 8-H, giving one positive partner and no other outside-band eigenvalues. The Watson elliptic integral has G0=(4pi)^-1 log(32/kappa)+O(kappa |log kappa|), while G0-Gr=Rr+O(kappa |log kappa|), yielding D=Rr/(2pi)log(32/kappa)-Rr^2+o(1), and the exact prefactor. At r=e1 the origin resolvent equation gives Rr=1/4. A reproducible high-precision check is included but not treated as proof.

value.rationale: Balanced attractive–repulsive defects have zero net potential yet bind for every coupling in two dimensions, at an anomalously smaller inverse-square-coupling exponential scale than an unbalanced attractive site. The theorem determines not only existence but both paired discrete levels for all coupling strengths, and explicitly identifies the intersite lattice resistance as the geometric invariant controlling the weak-binding exponent and prefactor for every fixed separation. This supplies meaningful quantitative and structural information for impurity localization beyond textbook one-site T-matrix calculations.
